title: The Genetics Podcast: How blood-based biomarkers are reshaping neurology
summary: Joe Volpe, Ph.D., executive director of scientific strategy & commercialization and neurology discipline director at Labcorp, joined The Genetics Podcast to discuss how blood-based biomarkers are advancing the field of neurology.
body_markdown:
Joe Volpe, Ph.D., executive director of scientific strategy & commercialization and neurology discipline director at Labcorp, joined *The Genetics Podcast* to discuss how blood-based biomarkers are advancing the field of neurology.


**Key takeaway:** Blood-based biomarkers are expanding the tools available to clinicians evaluating neurological conditions. Labcorp was the first U.S. company to launch both pTau-217 and neurofilament light chain (NfL) blood tests, helping advance access to biomarker testing in neurology.


Volpe explained that making new biomarkers available to clinicians early is essential to building familiarity and real-world experience. He noted that this approach helped support the incorporation of NfL into multiple sclerosis (MS) treatment guidelines and the label for an amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) therapy. He also discussed the scalability of pTau-217 testing, which can provide results nationwide from a simple blood draw within days.


**Why it matters:** Neurology has traditionally relied on imaging, clinical evaluation and specialized procedures. Blood-based biomarkers can provide additional information to support clinical decision-making and help broaden access to neurological insights through a simple blood draw.
